authority: Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 art.33 and art.34 — 8% employee and 17.5% employer, on a salary capped at 20 times the statutory reference level (2,340,000, ceiling 46,800,000). The employer 17.5% is 3% sickness and maternity, 14% retirement and survivorship, and 0.5% occupational accident and disease under the Law on Occupational Safety and Hygiene 84/2015/QH13 art.44 with Decree 58/2020/NĐ-CP art.4. Floor: Luật BHXH 41/2024/QH15 Điều 31(1)(đ) — tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,340,000 đ on this version). Applied 2026-09-18: an employer granted the reduced 0.3% occupational-accident rate (Decree 58/2020 art.5) records the entity fact `occupational_accident_reduced`; its share is then 17.3%. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH art.30(1)–(2): the insurance salary is the contractual salary plus the contractual allowances and fixed supplements (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a meal, fuel, phone or housing allowance is a row marked not fixed and stays outside. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Above the ceiling (twenty times the reference level) the employer’s share is the ceiling at the employer’s own rate — 17.3% where the occupational-accident fund is reduced (Decree 58/2020 art.4), 17.5% otherwise — the same choice the open rungs make. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): The base recorded is the insurance salary itself — the contractual salary floored at the reference level (2340000.0) and capped at twenty times it (46800000.0) — so a scheme that reads `produced.SI.base` reads the insured salary. Unpaid-leave continuation: Law 41/2024/QH15 arts.33(5) and 34(3) permit continuation by agreement at the most recent contribution base; art.31(1)(đ) sets the bounds at contribution time. The dated registration records the agreement, reference and prior base. Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.43(2) retains occupational-accident contributions on the compulsory SI salary. https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-luat-so-41-2024-qh15-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-119240723163650489.htm https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-158-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-bat-buoc-119250629171336803.htm Law 41/2024/QH15 art.33(5) limits the unpaid-month waiver to the listed categories, excluding part-time employees under art.2(1)(l); art.33(6) requires SI in the first working or return month with at least 14 sickness-benefit working days. Benefit eligibility and return-month status are dated declarations. BHXH letter 371/BHXH-QLT of 7 July 2025 section 1.2 counts a paid half-day as a working day; the threshold counts fully unpaid working dates, not summed wage-deduction fractions. https://cdn.thuvienphapluat.vn/uploads/Hoidapphapluat/2025/LNMT/Thang_7/250707/QLT-%C4%90VSDL%C4%90.pdf Maternity contributions: Law 41/2024/QH15 art.53(8) exempts birth, adoption under six months, surrogate-birth and commissioning-mother benefit leave without imposing 14 working days; other maternity-benefit cases are exempt only from 14 working days in the month. The dated eligibility and category elections distinguish statutory benefit leave from ordinary unpaid absence. Article 53(1), Circular 12/2025/TT-BNV art.9(4)(c) require compulsory SI after an early return from birth leave while the maternity allowance continues. Official application (birth leave starting 14 August 2025 is exempt that month): https://chinhsachonline.chinhphu.vn/xac-dinh-thoi-gian-lam-viec-de-dong-bhxh-82176.htm Circular: https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-thong-tu-12-2025-tt-bnv-quy-dinh-chi-tiet-mot-so-dieu-cua-luat-bhxh-ve-bhxh-bat-buoc-11925070415595016.htm Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Law 41/2024/QH15 art.2(7)(b) — a domestic worker (lao động là người giúp việc gia đình, `employment.type` DOMESTIC) is not a compulsory participant, so the SI base, and the union fund that reads it, is nil for one. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Law 41/2024 art.2(2)(b): a foreign employee at retirement age is measured at the contract’s signing against the age Decree 135/2020 art.4 sets for that year (men 60y3m in 2021 rising 3 months a year to 62 in 2028; women 55y4m in 2021 rising 4 months a year to 60 in 2035), read on `employment.service_start`.

rules.refusal: Record the employee as a Vietnamese citizen or a foreign national on the employment terms: compulsory social, health and unemployment insurance cover each on its own terms (Law 41/2024 art.2(1)–(2); Law 74/2025 art.31). A foreigner holding a permanent residence card is recorded as a foreign national.

Record the foreign employee’s gender and work permit type: Law 41/2024 art.2(2) covers a foreigner with a work permit, practising certificate or licence, except an intra-company transferee and one at retirement age (Labour Code 2019 art.169, which differs by gender).

name: Personal Income Tax (Thuế thu nhập cá nhân)
authority: Personal Income Tax Law 04/2007/QH12 and Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC; Law 109/2025/QH15 and Decree 253/2026/ND-CP for the 2026 rules. Declared non-residents receive 20% withholding on taxable remuneration without resident personal, dependant or insurance deductions; that rule precedes the resident short-contract withholding rule and does not require a rate override. Resident progressive withholding uses the version’s monthly scale and deduction amounts; the configured year-end rule reconciles annual withholding. Before 1 July 2026, non-residents retain the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out. The full qualifying overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026 arts.26 and 69). A future departure does not establish cessation in the current period. Payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Special tax profiles require further verification. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): Tax residence is a fact the employer records: a resident is present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or has a registered permanent residence or a rented home for 183 days or more (Decree 253/2026 art.4), and anyone else is non-resident (art.5); neither the Law nor the decree presumes either for an unknown residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation (`terms.tax_residency`). Residence governs the whole tax period (art.66(1)(a): the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival): each month is withheld on the status recorded for it (art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid), and a change of status during the year is settled in the annual finalisation, which re-prices the year’s wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20% (art.51; Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d)); earlier months are never re-withheld. Leave cash-out: art.26(2) exempts the pay for untaken leave only within the Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (the Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), and art.26(3) taxes the excess; income is taxed in the month it is paid (art.46(3)), so an excess is income of the paying month and is never spread over earlier periods. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Meal: Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(g.5) — a cash mid-shift meal is taxable only above the Labour Ministry cap of 730,000 a month (Circular 26/2016/TT-BLĐTBXH); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g) keeps 730,000 until art.69(1)(b) lifts it to 1,200,000 from 1 July 2026. A class counting toward PIT.MEAL enters the base only above that cap. Housing: rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf is taxable at the amount paid but not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit (Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(đ)(đ.1); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); a class counting toward PIT.HOUSING enters at the lower of the two. Voluntary pension and life insurance: deducted as paid, at most 1,000,000 a month, 12,000,000 a year (Circular 111/2013 art.9(2)(đ)), read from the dated VOLUNTARY_PENSION deduction claims. The art.49 medical, education and charity deductions are not withheld monthly: a taxpayer who claims them settles with the tax office personally (Decree 253/2026 art.51(3)), so the employer never applies them. Year-end: the December re-pricing on the annual table is the employer’s finalisation, which it may make only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies (Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d); Decree 253/2026 art.51(2)): the PIT election `finalisation_authorised`. Without it December is withheld on the monthly table. Night work: Circular 111/2013 art.3(1)(i) exempts only the part of night-work pay above the day wage — the night premium; the ordinary night hours stay in the salary base.

name: Social Insurance (Bảo hiểm xã hội)
authority: Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 art.33 and art.34 — 8% employee and 17.5% employer, on a salary capped at 20 times the statutory reference level (2,340,000, ceiling 46,800,000). The employer 17.5% is 3% sickness and maternity, 14% retirement and survivorship, and 0.5% occupational accident and disease under the Law on Occupational Safety and Hygiene 84/2015/QH13 art.44 with Decree 58/2020/NĐ-CP art.4. Floor: Luật BHXH 41/2024/QH15 Điều 31(1)(đ) — tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,340,000 đ on this version). Applied 2026-09-18: an employer granted the reduced 0.3% occupational-accident rate (Decree 58/2020 art.5) records the entity fact `occupational_accident_reduced`; its share is then 17.3%. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH art.30(1)–(2): the insurance salary is the contractual salary plus the contractual allowances and fixed supplements (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a meal, fuel, phone or housing allowance is a row marked not fixed and stays outside. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Above the ceiling (twenty times the reference level) the employer’s share is the ceiling at the employer’s own rate — 17.3% where the occupational-accident fund is reduced (Decree 58/2020 art.4), 17.5% otherwise — the same choice the open rungs make. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): The base recorded is the insurance salary itself — the contractual salary floored at the reference level (2340000.0) and capped at twenty times it (46800000.0) — so a scheme that reads `produced.SI.base` reads the insured salary. Unpaid-leave continuation: Law 41/2024/QH15 arts.33(5) and 34(3) permit continuation by agreement at the most recent contribution base; art.31(1)(đ) sets the bounds at contribution time. The dated registration records the agreement, reference and prior base. Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.43(2) retains occupational-accident contributions on the compulsory SI salary. https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-luat-so-41-2024-qh15-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-119240723163650489.htm https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-158-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-bat-buoc-119250629171336803.htm Law 41/2024/QH15 art.33(5) limits the unpaid-month waiver to the listed categories, excluding part-time employees under art.2(1)(l); art.33(6) requires SI in the first working or return month with at least 14 sickness-benefit working days. Benefit eligibility and return-month status are dated declarations. BHXH letter 371/BHXH-QLT of 7 July 2025 section 1.2 counts a paid half-day as a working day; the threshold counts fully unpaid working dates, not summed wage-deduction fractions. https://cdn.thuvienphapluat.vn/uploads/Hoidapphapluat/2025/LNMT/Thang_7/250707/QLT-%C4%90VSDL%C4%90.pdf Maternity contributions: Law 41/2024/QH15 art.53(8) exempts birth, adoption under six months, surrogate-birth and commissioning-mother benefit leave without imposing 14 working days; other maternity-benefit cases are exempt only from 14 working days in the month. The dated eligibility and category elections distinguish statutory benefit leave from ordinary unpaid absence. Article 53(1), Circular 12/2025/TT-BNV art.9(4)(c) require compulsory SI after an early return from birth leave while the maternity allowance continues. Official application (birth leave starting 14 August 2025 is exempt that month): https://chinhsachonline.chinhphu.vn/xac-dinh-thoi-gian-lam-viec-de-dong-bhxh-82176.htm Circular: https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-thong-tu-12-2025-tt-bnv-quy-dinh-chi-tiet-mot-so-dieu-cua-luat-bhxh-ve-bhxh-bat-buoc-11925070415595016.htm Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Law 41/2024/QH15 art.2(7)(b) — a domestic worker (lao động là người giúp việc gia đình, `employment.type` DOMESTIC) is not a compulsory participant, so the SI base, and the union fund that reads it, is nil for one. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Law 41/2024 art.2(2)(b): a foreign employee at retirement age is measured at the contract’s signing against the age Decree 135/2020 art.4 sets for that year (men 60y3m in 2021 rising 3 months a year to 62 in 2028; women 55y4m in 2021 rising 4 months a year to 60 in 2035), read on `employment.service_start`.

authority: Law on Employment 74/2025/QH15 arts.31 to 33, in force 1 January 2026 — 1% of the employee's monthly wage and 1% of the employer's monthly wage fund, on a wage capped at 20 times the regional minimum wage (Decree 293/2025/NĐ-CP). name: Personal Income Tax (Thuế thu nhập cá nhân)
authority: Personal Income Tax Law 04/2007/QH12 and Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC; Law 109/2025/QH15 and Decree 253/2026/ND-CP for the 2026 rules. Declared non-residents receive 20% withholding on taxable remuneration without resident personal, dependant or insurance deductions; that rule precedes the resident short-contract withholding rule and does not require a rate override. Resident progressive withholding uses the version’s monthly scale and deduction amounts; the configured year-end rule reconciles annual withholding. Before 1 July 2026, non-residents retain the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out. The full qualifying overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026 arts.26 and 69). A future departure does not establish cessation in the current period. Payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Special tax profiles require further verification. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): Tax residence is a fact the employer records: a resident is present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or has a registered permanent residence or a rented home for 183 days or more (Decree 253/2026 art.4), and anyone else is non-resident (art.5); neither the Law nor the decree presumes either for an unknown residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation (`terms.tax_residency`). Residence governs the whole tax period (art.66(1)(a): the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival): each month is withheld on the status recorded for it (art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid), and a change of status during the year is settled in the annual finalisation, which re-prices the year’s wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20% (art.51; Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d)); earlier months are never re-withheld. Leave cash-out: art.26(2) exempts the pay for untaken leave only within the Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (the Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), and art.26(3) taxes the excess; income is taxed in the month it is paid (art.46(3)), so an excess is income of the paying month and is never spread over earlier periods. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Meal: Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(g.5) — a cash mid-shift meal is taxable only above the Labour Ministry cap of 730,000 a month (Circular 26/2016/TT-BLĐTBXH); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g) keeps 730,000 until art.69(1)(b) lifts it to 1,200,000 from 1 July 2026. A class counting toward PIT.MEAL enters the base only above that cap. Housing: rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf is taxable at the amount paid but not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit (Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(đ)(đ.1); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); a class counting toward PIT.HOUSING enters at the lower of the two. Voluntary pension and life insurance: deducted as paid, at most 3,000,000 a month in total including the employer’s share, from tax year 2026 (Decree 253/2026 art.46(2)(a) with art.69(1)(a)), read from the dated VOLUNTARY_PENSION deduction claims; the annual settlement allows twelve months’ cap. The art.49 medical, education and charity deductions are not withheld monthly: a taxpayer who claims them settles with the tax office personally (Decree 253/2026 art.51(3)), so the employer never applies them. Year-end: the December re-pricing on the annual table is the employer’s finalisation, which it may make only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies (Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d); Decree 253/2026 art.51(2)): the PIT election `finalisation_authorised`. Without it December is withheld on the monthly table. Night work: Decree 253/2026 art.26(1) exempts "tiền lương, tiền công làm việc ban đêm" — the wage for night work itself, where Circular 111/2013 art.3(1)(i) exempted only "phần tiền lương, tiền công trả cao hơn" the day wage; Decree 145/2020 art.56 prices the night-work wage as the ordinary hour × night hours plus at least 30% of it. The ordinary night hours' share of the salary (`NIGHT_WAGE`) leaves the base beside the premium for residents (non-residents keep the premium-only exemption until 1 July 2026, art.69(1)).

name: Social Insurance (Bảo hiểm xã hội)
authority: Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 art.33 and art.34 — 8% employee and 17.5% employer, on a salary capped at 20 times the statutory reference level (2,530,000, ceiling 50,600,000). The employer 17.5% is 3% sickness and maternity, 14% retirement and survivorship, and 0.5% occupational accident and disease under the Law on Occupational Safety and Hygiene 84/2015/QH13 art.44 with Decree 58/2020/NĐ-CP art.4. Floor: Luật BHXH 41/2024/QH15 Điều 31(1)(đ) — tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,530,000 đ on this version). Applied 2026-09-18: an employer granted the reduced 0.3% occupational-accident rate (Decree 58/2020 art.5) records the entity fact `occupational_accident_reduced`; its share is then 17.3%. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH art.30(1)–(2): the insurance salary is the contractual salary plus the contractual allowances and fixed supplements (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a meal, fuel, phone or housing allowance is a row marked not fixed and stays outside. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Above the ceiling (twenty times the reference level) the employer’s share is the ceiling at the employer’s own rate — 17.3% where the occupational-accident fund is reduced (Decree 58/2020 art.4), 17.5% otherwise — the same choice the open rungs make. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): The base recorded is the insurance salary itself — the contractual salary floored at the reference level (2530000.0) and capped at twenty times it (50600000.0) — so a scheme that reads `produced.SI.base` reads the insured salary. Unpaid-leave continuation: Law 41/2024/QH15 arts.33(5) and 34(3) permit continuation by agreement at the most recent contribution base; art.31(1)(đ) sets the bounds at contribution time. The dated registration records the agreement, reference and prior base. Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.43(2) retains occupational-accident contributions on the compulsory SI salary. https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-luat-so-41-2024-qh15-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-119240723163650489.htm https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-158-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-bat-buoc-119250629171336803.htm Law 41/2024/QH15 art.33(5) limits the unpaid-month waiver to the listed categories, excluding part-time employees under art.2(1)(l); art.33(6) requires SI in the first working or return month with at least 14 sickness-benefit working days. Benefit eligibility and return-month status are dated declarations. BHXH letter 371/BHXH-QLT of 7 July 2025 section 1.2 counts a paid half-day as a working day; the threshold counts fully unpaid working dates, not summed wage-deduction fractions. https://cdn.thuvienphapluat.vn/uploads/Hoidapphapluat/2025/LNMT/Thang_7/250707/QLT-%C4%90VSDL%C4%90.pdf Maternity contributions: Law 41/2024/QH15 art.53(8) exempts birth, adoption under six months, surrogate-birth and commissioning-mother benefit leave without imposing 14 working days; other maternity-benefit cases are exempt only from 14 working days in the month. authority: Personal Income Tax Law 04/2007/QH12 and Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC; Law 109/2025/QH15 and Decree 253/2026/ND-CP for the 2026 rules. Declared non-residents receive 20% withholding on taxable remuneration without resident personal, dependant or insurance deductions; that rule precedes the resident short-contract withholding rule and does not require a rate override. Resident progressive withholding uses the version’s monthly scale and deduction amounts; the configured year-end rule reconciles annual withholding. Before 1 July 2026, non-residents retain the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out. The full qualifying overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026 arts.26 and 69). A future departure does not establish cessation in the current period. Payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Special tax profiles require further verification. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): Tax residence is a fact the employer records: a resident is present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or has a registered permanent residence or a rented home for 183 days or more (Decree 253/2026 art.4), and anyone else is non-resident (art.5); neither the Law nor the decree presumes either for an unknown residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation (`terms.tax_residency`). Residence governs the whole tax period (art.66(1)(a): the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival): each month is withheld on the status recorded for it (art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid), and a change of status during the year is settled in the annual finalisation, which re-prices the year’s wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20% (art.51; Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d)); earlier months are never re-withheld. Leave cash-out: art.26(2) exempts the pay for untaken leave only within the Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (the Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), and art.26(3) taxes the excess; income is taxed in the month it is paid (art.46(3)), so an excess is income of the paying month and is never spread over earlier periods. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Meal: Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g) with art.69(1)(b) — from 1 July 2026 a meal paid by the employer is taxable only above 1,200,000 a month; a meal served in kind is not income. A class counting toward PIT.MEAL enters the base only above that cap. Housing: rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf is taxable at the amount paid but not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit (Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(đ)(đ.1); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); a class counting toward PIT.HOUSING enters at the lower of the two. Voluntary pension and life insurance: deducted as paid, at most 3,000,000 a month in total including the employer’s share, from tax year 2026 (Decree 253/2026 art.46(2)(a) with art.69(1)(a)), read from the dated VOLUNTARY_PENSION deduction claims; the annual settlement allows twelve months’ cap. The art.49 medical, education and charity deductions are not withheld monthly: a taxpayer who claims them settles with the tax office personally (Decree 253/2026 art.51(3)), so the employer never applies them. Year-end: the December re-pricing on the annual table is the employer’s finalisation, which it may make only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies (Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d); Decree 253/2026 art.51(2)): the PIT election `finalisation_authorised`. Without it December is withheld on the monthly table. Night work: Decree 253/2026 art.26(1) exempts "tiền lương, tiền công làm việc ban đêm" — the wage for night work itself, where Circular 111/2013 art.3(1)(i) exempted only "phần tiền lương, tiền công trả cao hơn" the day wage; Decree 145/2020 art.56 prices the night-work wage as the ordinary hour × night hours plus at least 30% of it. The ordinary night hours' share of the salary (`NIGHT_WAGE`) leaves the base beside the premium for every employee.

name: Social Insurance (Bảo hiểm xã hội)
authority: Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 art.33 and art.34 — 8% employee and 17.5% employer, on a salary capped at 20 times the statutory reference level (2,340,000, ceiling 46,800,000). The employer 17.5% is 3% sickness and maternity, 14% retirement and survivorship, and 0.5% occupational accident and disease under the Law on Occupational Safety and Hygiene 84/2015/QH13 art.44 with Decree 58/2020/NĐ-CP art.4. Floor: Luật BHXH 41/2024/QH15 Điều 31(1)(đ) — tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,340,000 đ on this version). Applied 2026-09-18: an employer granted the reduced 0.3% occupational-accident rate (Decree 58/2020 art.5) records the entity fact `occupational_accident_reduced`; its share is then 17.3%. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH art.30(1)–(2): the insurance salary is the contractual salary plus the contractual allowances and fixed supplements (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a meal, fuel, phone or housing allowance is a row marked not fixed and stays outside. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Above the ceiling (twenty times the reference level) the employer’s share is the ceiling at the employer’s own rate — 17.3% where the occupational-accident fund is reduced (Decree 58/2020 art.4), 17.5% otherwise — the same choice the open rungs make. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): The base recorded is the insurance salary itself — the contractual salary floored at the reference level (2340000.0) and capped at twenty times it (46800000.0) — so a scheme that reads `produced.SI.base` reads the insured salary. Unpaid-leave continuation: Law 41/2024/QH15 arts.33(5) and 34(3) permit continuation by agreement at the most recent contribution base; art.31(1)(đ) sets the bounds at contribution time. The dated registration records the agreement, reference and prior base. Decree 158/2025/NĐ-CP art.43(2) retains occupational-accident contributions on the compulsory SI salary. https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-luat-so-41-2024-qh15-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-119240723163650489.htm https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-nghi-dinh-158-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-bat-buoc-119250629171336803.htm Law 41/2024/QH15 art.33(5) limits the unpaid-month waiver to the listed categories, excluding part-time employees under art.2(1)(l); art.33(6) requires SI in the first working or return month with at least 14 sickness-benefit working days. Benefit eligibility and return-month status are dated declarations. BHXH letter 371/BHXH-QLT of 7 July 2025 section 1.2 counts a paid half-day as a working day; the threshold counts fully unpaid working dates, not summed wage-deduction fractions. https://cdn.thuvienphapluat.vn/uploads/Hoidapphapluat/2025/LNMT/Thang_7/250707/QLT-%C4%90VSDL%C4%90.pdf Maternity contributions: Law 41/2024/QH15 art.53(8) exempts birth, adoption under six months, surrogate-birth and commissioning-mother benefit leave without imposing 14 working days; other maternity-benefit cases are exempt only from 14 working days in the month. The dated eligibility and category elections distinguish statutory benefit leave from ordinary unpaid absence. Article 53(1), Circular 12/2025/TT-BNV art.9(4)(c) require compulsory SI after an early return from birth leave while the maternity allowance continues. Official application (birth leave starting 14 August 2025 is exempt that month): https://chinhsachonline.chinhphu.vn/xac-dinh-thoi-gian-lam-viec-de-dong-bhxh-82176.htm Circular: https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-thong-tu-12-2025-tt-bnv-quy-dinh-chi-tiet-mot-so-dieu-cua-luat-bhxh-ve-bhxh-bat-buoc-11925070415595016.htm Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Law 41/2024/QH15 art.2(7)(b) — a domestic worker (lao động là người giúp việc gia đình, `employment.type` DOMESTIC) is not a compulsory participant, so the SI base, and the union fund that reads it, is nil for one. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Law 41/2024 art.2(2)(b): a foreign employee at retirement age is measured at the contract’s signing against the age Decree 135/2020 art.4 sets for that year (men 60y3m in 2021 rising 3 months a year to 62 in 2028; women 55y4m in 2021 rising 4 months a year to 60 in 2035), read on `employment.service_start`.

authority: Trade Union Law 50/2024/QH15 art.29 with Decision 1908/QĐ-TLĐ art.23: a union member pays dues of 1% of the salary the social-insurance contribution is based on, capped at 10% of the reference (base) salary; paid to the union, never by a non-member. The `union_member` election says who is one. Applied 2026-09-18. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH art.30(1)–(2): the insurance salary is the contractual salary plus the contractual allowances and fixed supplements (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a meal, fuel, phone or housing allowance is a row marked not fixed and stays outside. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Quyết định 61/QĐ-TLĐ of the Vietnam General Confederation of Labour, in force from 1 July 2025, cut the dues of a member in an enterprise outside the State sector to 0.5% of the salary the compulsory social insurance is based on, capped at 10% of the base salary (mức lương cơ sở) — the 1% of Decision 1908/QĐ-TLĐ no longer stands on any version here. https://pbgdpl.cantho.gov.vn/quyet-dinh-61qd-tld-ve-dieu-chinh-giam-muc-dong-doan-phi-cong-doan https://nhandan.vn/chinh-thuc-giam-muc-dong-doan-phi-cong-doan-tu-172025-post898504.html

name: Health Insurance (Bảo hiểm y tế)
authority: Law on Health Insurance 25/2008/QH12 art.13 as amended by Law 51/2024/QH15, in force 1 July 2025, with Decree 146/2018/NĐ-CP — 4.5% of the salary, split 1.5% employee and 3% employer, on the same 20 times reference level ceiling as social insurance (46,800,000). Floor: Luật BHXH 41/2024/QH15 Điều 31(1)(đ) — tiền lương làm căn cứ đóng thấp nhất bằng mức tham chiếu (2,340,000 đ on this version). Applied 2026-09-18 (4): Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH art.30(1)–(2): the insurance salary is the contractual salary plus the contractual allowances and fixed supplements (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a meal, fuel, phone or housing allowance is a row marked not fixed and stays outside. Applied 2026-09-19 (3): The base recorded is the insurance salary itself — the contractual salary floored at the reference level (2340000.0) and capped at twenty times it (46800000.0) — so a scheme that reads `produced.HI.base` reads the insured salary. Where an unpaid-leave agreement continues compulsory SI, health insurance continues on that SI base. Vietnam Social Security guidance, 18 June 2026: https://baohiemxahoi.gov.vn/tintuc/Pages/linh-vuc-bao-hiem-xa-hoi.aspx?CateID=168&ItemID=26671 Health Insurance Law art.12(2)(b), as amended by Law 51/2024/QH15 from 1 July 2025, transfers HI payment to the social-insurance fund for at least 14 sickness-benefit working days, or benefit leave for a listed long-term illness. This remains fund-paid when SI is mandatory in the first working or return month or voluntarily continued. https://congbao.cdnchinhphu.vn/CongBaoCP/VanBan/2025/2/44464/55506-1-2025539-54022-vbhn-vpqh.pdf Law 41/2024/QH15 arts.8(2)(b) and 84(2)(c), with Health Insurance Law art.12(2)(b) as amended by Law 51/2024/QH15, transfer HI payment to the social-insurance fund only for maternity-benefit leave of at least 14 working days in the month. An early return resumes payroll HI; shorter special-category leave can be SI-exempt under art.53(8) while payroll HI remains due. rules.refusal: Record the employee as a Vietnamese citizen or a foreign national on the employment terms: compulsory social, health and unemployment insurance cover each on its own terms (Law 41/2024 art.2(1)–(2); Law 74/2025 art.31). name: Unemployment Insurance (Bảo hiểm thất nghiệp)
authority: Law on Employment 74/2025/QH15 arts.31 to 33, in force 1 January 2026 — 1% of the employee's monthly wage and 1% of the employer's monthly wage fund, on a wage capped at 20 times the regional minimum wage (Decree 293/2025/NĐ-CP). The scheme covers Vietnamese employees; a foreign employee is outside it. Applied 2026-09-18 (4): Circular 06/2021/TT-BLĐTBXH art.30(1)–(2): the insurance salary is the contractual salary plus the contractual allowances and fixed supplements (`terms.fixed_allowances`, the standing rows marked fixed); a meal, fuel, phone or housing allowance is a row marked not fixed and stays outside. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Law 41/2024 art.31(1)(đ) makes the unemployment-insurance base the social-insurance base, so its floor is the version’s reference level — 2,530,000 from 1 July 2026 as for SI, not the earlier 2,340,000. Law 74/2025/QH15 article 33(4) separately exempts months with at least 14 unpaid working days from UI; an SI continuation agreement does not remove that exemption. https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-luat-viec-lam-119250711173403835.htm Fully unpaid working dates determine the unpaid-day threshold; a paid half-day remains a working day under BHXH letter 371/BHXH-QLT of 7 July 2025 section 1.2. Law 74/2025/QH15 art.33(4), effective 1 January 2026, exempts UI only when the worker has at least 14 working days without salary; the special SI maternity categories do not create a shorter UI exemption. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): a domestic worker is outside unemployment insurance — Law 38/2013/QH13 art.43(1) to 31 December 2025, Law 74/2025/QH15 art.31(2) from 1 January 2026 (`employment.type` DOMESTIC). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Law 74/2025 art.31(2) excludes an employee who already qualifies for a pension, not only one drawing it — the UI election `pension_qualified`. Foreign employees: Law 41/2024 art.2(2)(b) measures retirement age at the contract’s signing, against the age Decree 135/2020 art.4 sets for that year (men 60y3m in 2021 rising 3 months a year to 62 in 2028; women 55y4m in 2021 rising 4 months a year to 60 in 2035).

name: Personal Income Tax (Thuế thu nhập cá nhân)
authority: Personal Income Tax Law 04/2007/QH12 and Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC; Law 109/2025/QH15 and Decree 253/2026/ND-CP for the 2026 rules. Declared non-residents receive 20% withholding on taxable remuneration without resident personal, dependant or insurance deductions; that rule precedes the resident short-contract withholding rule and does not require a rate override. Resident progressive withholding uses the version’s monthly scale and deduction amounts; the configured year-end rule reconciles annual withholding. Before 1 July 2026, non-residents retain the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out. The full qualifying overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026 arts.26 and 69). A future departure does not establish cessation in the current period. Payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Special tax profiles require further verification. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 4): Tax residence is a fact the employer records: a resident is present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or has a registered permanent residence or a rented home for 183 days or more (Decree 253/2026 art.4), and anyone else is non-resident (art.5); neither the Law nor the decree presumes either for an unknown residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation (`terms.tax_residency`). Residence governs the whole tax period (art.66(1)(a): the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival): each month is withheld on the status recorded for it (art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid), and a change of status during the year is settled in the annual finalisation, which re-prices the year’s wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20% (art.51; Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d)); earlier months are never re-withheld. Leave cash-out: art.26(2) exempts the pay for untaken leave only within the Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (the Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), and art.26(3) taxes the excess; income is taxed in the month it is paid (art.46(3)), so an excess is income of the paying month and is never spread over earlier periods. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): Meal: Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(g.5) — a cash mid-shift meal is taxable only above the Labour Ministry cap of 730,000 a month (Circular 26/2016/TT-BLĐTBXH); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g) keeps 730,000 until art.69(1)(b) lifts it to 1,200,000 from 1 July 2026. A class counting toward PIT.MEAL enters the base only above that cap. Housing: rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf is taxable at the amount paid but not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit (Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(đ)(đ.1); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); a class counting toward PIT.HOUSING enters at the lower of the two. Voluntary pension and life insurance: deducted as paid, at most 3,000,000 a month in total including the employer’s share, from tax year 2026 (Decree 253/2026 art.46(2)(a) with art.69(1)(a)), read from the dated VOLUNTARY_PENSION deduction claims; the annual settlement allows twelve months’ cap. The art.49 medical, education and charity deductions are not withheld monthly: a taxpayer who claims them settles with the tax office personally (Decree 253/2026 art.51(3)), so the employer never applies them. Year-end: the December re-pricing on the annual table is the employer’s finalisation, which it may make only for an employee who authorised it and qualifies (Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d); Decree 253/2026 art.51(2)): the PIT election `finalisation_authorised`. Without it December is withheld on the monthly table. Night work: Decree 253/2026 art.26(1) exempts "tiền lương, tiền công làm việc ban đêm" — the wage for night work itself, where Circular 111/2013 art.3(1)(i) exempted only "phần tiền lương, tiền công trả cao hơn" the day wage; Decree 145/2020 art.56 prices the night-work wage as the ordinary hour × night hours plus at least 30% of it. The ordinary night hours' share of the salary (`NIGHT_WAGE`) leaves the base beside the premium for residents (non-residents keep the premium-only exemption until 1 July 2026, art.69(1)).
